title: An ordinary henselization at a prime is ind-etale over the original ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be a prime ideal, and let $H$ be an ordinary henselization of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Then the canonical composite $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to H$ is ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04GN (lemma-henselization), property (2), applied to A_p; the extension to A uses the filtered principal-localization presentation of A_p and ind-etale composition. The universal-property convention is Tag 04GQ (definition-henselization).

proof.text: Put R=A_p and m=maximalIdeal R. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] to obtain essential smallness and filteredness of the category E of etale R-algebras inducing an isomorphism modulo m. Take I to be the skeleton of its universe-u small model, and e:I ≌ E the resulting equivalence. Filteredness passes along e. Construct the actual categorical colimit c of e followed by the inclusion into Under R. The forgetful functor to rings preserves this connected colimit, by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]. Apply [lem-trf-prime-pair-colimit-ind-etale-model] to this specified cocone. It supplies a henselian local structure on C=c.pt, locality of its R-map, the equality maximalIdeal C=mC, bijectivity of the structural quotient map, and ind-etaleness of both R→C and the specified composite A→C.

Identify C/mC with its residue field using the supplied equality of ideals. The structural quotient map is then exactly the residue map of the local structure map R→C. The hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] supplies locality of R→H and the initial local-map property. Apply [lem-trf-initial-henselian-colimit-comparison] to R,C,H. Retain its R-algebra maps f:C→H and g:H→C with gf=id and fg=id. These identities prove directly that f is bijective.

A bijective ring map is etale and hence ind-etale: use the singleton presentation, equivalently Mathlib MorphismProperty.le_ind. Composing the ind-etale map A→C with f gives an ind-etale map A→H. Since f is an R-algebra map, this composite equals exactly A→R→H. The helper conclusions use [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] in its ULift form. For rings in the same universe, descend that form by pre- and postcomposing with the canonical bijective ULift ring maps, using ind-etale composition. Thus the conclusion has precisely the original RingHom.IndEtale predicate. This elementary isomorphism-invariance argument avoids expanding or transporting the presentation again.
